slides.3.title: Beira Interior: The Three Sub-DOCs
slides.3.html:
Beira Interior DOC is the main region of Portugal's central highlands, next to the Serra da Estrela (over 2,000m) and the Spanish border.

🗺️ Three sub-region DOCs

  • Castelo Rodrigo: the northernmost, close to Spain's Castilla. The most extreme continental climate, mainly Touriga Nacional and Marufo, with deep colour and intensity
  • Pinhel: central, granite soils and cooler, with outstanding crisp whites (Fonte Cal, Siria)
  • Cova da Beira: the southernmost, valley terrain sheltered by the Serra da Estrela; the largest sub-region, producing both red and white

🌡️ Climate

  • Dominated by a continental climate: summer highs of 35–38°C, winter lows down to -5°C
  • Annual rainfall of 500–700mm, drier than the Dão
  • Strong temperature swings help preserve the grapes' natural acidity

🍇 Main grapes

  • Red: Touriga Nacional・Rufete・Marufo・Tinta Amarela
  • White: Siria (= Roupeiro)・Fonte Cal・Arinto
slides.4.question: Which three sub-regions does the Beira Interior DOC include?
slides.4.explanation: The Beira Interior DOC includes three sub-regions: Castelo Rodrigo (the northernmost, most extreme continental), Pinhel (central, granite, excellent whites) and Cova da Beira (the southernmost, valley, the largest). All three lie next to the Serra da Estrela and the Spanish border.
slides.5.question: In Beira Interior, which is a rare native red grape that is almost never seen in other regions?
slides.5.explanation: Rufete is a native red grape specific to Beira Interior (especially Castelo Rodrigo), medium-bodied with red berry fruit and spice, and extremely rare in other Portuguese regions. It is a precious legacy of Portugal's varietal diversity.
